## last-piece-lazy

Selected evaluation: lazy candidates, remaining-piece inputs and solution tree.

## Algorithm and workload

Tile the fixed 8x8 board using the source's sex-constrained piece orientations.
Start with the three-square a piece, scan row-major from (1,2) Female, choose a
remaining piece/orientation, fit it into a persistent board map, and recursively
construct Soln/Choose/Fail search results. Render every solution in source order.
The full puzzle has three solutions; retain the exact piece data and ordering.

## History, revision, authorship and dependencies

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798,
spectral/last-piece/Main.hs, Makefile and last-piece.stdout. The header credits
Simon Peyton Jones, May 2002. It states no separate redistribution notice;
retain the original without inventing a grant from another component.

Original GHC 9.4.7 uses containers 0.6.7 and pretty 1.1.3.6. Pin containers at
9f4a93604c66a5e605ce46fc30003b71802b3cfd and pretty at
c3a1469306b35fa5d023dc570554f97f1a90435d. Retain complete selected source files,
package versions and BSD-style notices. Map source credits Daan Leijen and
Andriy Palamarchuk; the rendering module credits Glasgow and the Hughes/
Peyton Jones design. The explicit last-piece-lazy/strict names preserve
meaningful search-tree evaluation variants.

## Source ordering, preconditions and variants

pickOne reverses the skipped prefix: choices for [a,b,c] leave [b,c], [a,c],
then [b,a]. Do not replace it with the usual stable-order deletion. Orientations
retain their exact order and share the remaining-piece thunk for one piece.
Fitting checks offsets first and inserts the anchor last without another bounds/
occupancy check. Source search establishes that anchor precondition; direct fit
is not silently strengthened. Row transitions and occupied squares flip sex
exactly as written. Selected offsets keep rows positive, so the source's absent
lower-row guard is not added.

The lazy variant memoizes candidate/result spines and solution children, fitting
one candidate before demanding its recursive search. Rendering visits all
solutions/failures in the source order. The strict variant constructs finite
candidates and the complete result tree eagerly, retaining the same board-map
algorithm and output. Both agree on full outputs; their temporary allocation,
retention and evaluation timing differ.

## Portable SML translation

SML97 keeps the size-balanced persistent map with cached subtree sizes,
delta3/ratio2 and the source's specialized balanceL/balanceR rotations. Every
insertion-prefix shape agrees with original containers on four 64-key traces.
It is not replaced with an AVL or mutable occupancy array. Native pointer-
equality insertion shortcuts are omitted: benchmark insertions use fresh keys,
so those early returns cannot occur. General replacement values preserve map
contents/shape without claiming identical pointer-identity optimizations.

Board keys, offsets, sizes and counts fit signed 31-bit Int. Piece identifiers
are the original ASCII characters. Remaining-piece and orientation lists retain
their values; candidate/result nodes and shared remaining lists use explicit
memoized delays where needed. Immutable piece data/initial board may be shared;
each solve call reconstructs the result tree, preventing previous solutions
from being reused as a repeated-run result cache.

The used-domain renderer replaces the external pretty library with portable
SML emission. Fixed board lines fit width200 and ribbon ratio1.5; no wrapping
alternative is exercised. Preserve Success!, reverse row display, two-space
nesting, indented blank lines and the final newline, including empty-result
behavior. This is not a claimed port of every general pretty API. Full byte/EOF
checking and reference I/O replace stdout and are measured work. The driver
reports remaining:solutions:bytes only after complete validation.

## Profiles and diagnostic questions

Smoke leaves the last two source pieces and preplaces the others from the first
reviewed original solution. This is a valid subproblem through the original
search API, with the same board size, initial a, sex and orientation rules.
Normal preserves all 13 remaining pieces and the original three solutions.
An eight-piece subproblem is also retained as a correctness reference. The
fixed original board is already the maximum source instance, so no artificial
large profile is introduced; the harness still supports explicit repeated mode.
The driver bounds remaining pieces to 0..13. SML generates runtime board inputs
from exact embedded data; no external dataset or input-generating interpreter
is required.

Source-based questions include map rotation/allocation, failed fits, reversed
choice order, memoized search, eager result retention and rendering/check costs.
These remain hypotheses until source/measurement evidence establishes effects.
Standard reports compare identical SML. No parallelism, FFI, effects or compiler/
runtime feature is required.

## References and validation

The unmodified original's complete 300-byte output matches the pinned fixture.
Original prefix calls and an independent bitmask/reversed-choice model agree on
all boards and exact output for 0/2/8/13 remaining pieces. The full model visits
103513 search states and finds three solutions; original tree statistics agree.
Every board covers all 64 squares. The smoke/normal inputs are not fabricated
by merely dropping pieces from an empty board.

Tests cover 256 complete map-prefix shapes, initial board, reversed pickOne,
shared/delayed remaining pieces, unforced child search, source fit preconditions,
complete prefix outputs/statistics and changed/truncated/extra output rejection.
Both SML variants reproduce the full original output in bounded preflights.
Large or other configuration validation is claimed only where recorded.
Pinned source and dependency explanations provide the exact implementation
reference; the shared nofib/measurement literature supplies context without
claiming a measured performance cause for this translation.

[Complete provenance](last-piece-lazy/PROVENANCE.md).

## boyer-nofib-lazy

Selected finite term/argument evaluation: lazy; recursive lemma streams remain memoized.

## Algorithm and workload

Apply the source substitution to its transitivity theorem, recursively rewrite
terms with attached function lemmas, and check the resulting conditional form.
Terms are typed Var IDs or Fun IDs/arguments/lemmas; equality deliberately ignores
lemma fields. Preserve one-way unification, variable binding order, rewrite
priority, conditional assumptions and short circuiting. The source Main performs
100 repetitions; each test checks n instances from an opaque repeated Var X list.

## History, revision, authorship and aliases

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/boyer/Main.lhs,
Makefile and three stdout fixtures. The header names Bob Boyer, Bob Shaw and
Will Clinger, and credits Denis Howe's July1992 Scheme-to-Haskell conversion.
Its Status explicitly says Public Domain; retain the complete notice/history.
The included Scheme listing is comparison material, not a second executable.
The source notes that some unused Scheme lemmas were not translated.

Classic SML boyer keeps the unsuffixed name. These variants use
boyer-nofib-lazy/strict. The other nofib boyer2 uses textual Lisp parsing and an
unbalanced LUT, with different rule data/input quirks. Do not merge its binary
Lisp implementation with this typed-ID/per-Fun-lemma representation merely
because both ultimately prove the transitivity statement.

## Lazy graph, strict variant and exact behavior

The lazy variant memoizes term/argument heads and spines. Each function's
invariant lemmas are represented by one shared memoized rule stream; terms
retain the attached stream pointer. This explicit rule graph remains lazy in
both variants because constant/function lemmas refer recursively to their own
function nodes. Strict term/argument construction does not force those cyclic
rule fields. Unused rules are not normalized eagerly (for example, the unused
unconditional gcd swap is not a new terminating API).

Failed unification/find results keep their delayed error field. Matching tests
the Boolean before demanding the environment. Argument matching requires both
lists to end, unlike boyer2's source prefix rule. Substitution copies the original
lemma pointer; term equality traverses IDs/arguments without touching it.
The strict variant eagerly constructs finite term/argument structure while
retaining the necessary memoized graph and failed-result control. Results agree.

## Portable translation and input generation

SML97 uses closed enum codes for all50 IDs (nine variables, 41 functions),
retaining exact names/mapping and constant-time ID equality. Generated constructor
functions preserve the original finite ASTs; argument factories defer child
construction in the lazy variant. No runtime text parser or different symbolic
term encoding is inserted into the kernel. Rule/theorem/substitution data are
extracted with export-only Haskell observers; original source and generation
scripts are retained. The extraction adds Show/exports and exposes the original
where bindings without changing numeric/rewriting expressions.

The runtime variable file replaces source NOINLINE xs with an opaque portable
input dependency. It starts with a repetition count, followed by one variable-
name row per test. The selected rows contain exactly the source's repeated X;
the parser permits every original variable ID so it does not reveal a constant
X to the optimizer before computing. SML97 generation writes these fixed rows.
Input I/O/name parsing is an explicit added driver cost. A valid result checks
every theorem before reporting repetitions:proofs:proved instead of 100 True
lines. Bounds are 1..100 repetitions and at most75 variables per row. Counter/
ID/list sizes fit 31-bit Int; no machine-width arithmetic is silently changed.

## Profiles, checks and diagnostic questions

Smoke preserves FAST2 per test, normal NORM15, and selected large SLOW75; all
preserve 100 source repetitions. Immutable rule/input constants may be shared,
while every theorem construction/substitution/rewrite is invoked through its
runtime variable. No previous theorem result is cached as a repeated-run answer.
No dataset or external runtime feature is required.

Original complete outputs match all three fixtures. Original and independent
models agree on the full instantiated input and 170284-byte normalized form for
X. All nine variable inputs are checked independently over all32 truth
assignments: only X is a tautology. Complete SML lazy/strict forms agree byte
for byte. These supplemental observations force full results only in tests,
not in the timed Boolean consumer. Tests cover graph-safe equality, unification
bottoms/short circuiting, exact argument lengths and wrong/truncated/extra forms.

Source-based questions include enum dispatch, attached-rule sharing, recursive
argument demand, failed matches, eager unused terms, input setup and invariant
specialization. They remain hypotheses until supported by inspection or
measurements. Standard reports compare identical SML; Haskell is a correctness
reference. Large execution is claimed only where recorded.

## Literature and source explanations

The retained literate program explains why its theorem/substitution are chosen,
how typed terms differ from the Scheme property-list representation, and which
setup work belongs to that original comparison. Gabriel's Performance and
Evaluation of Lisp Systems supplies the benchmark's historical context, and
the nofib/measurement survey frames current comparisons. Historical remarks
about language advantages or costs do not establish current SML rankings.

[Complete provenance](boyer-nofib-lazy/PROVENANCE.md).

## eliza-lazy

Selected finite candidate/output evaluation: lazy; cyclic reply queues remain memoized.

## Algorithm and workload

Run the source's ordered keyword/tail search and cyclic response selection over
its fixed conversation. Trim only space, period, exclamation mark, question mark
and comma from line ends; split into words and discard empty lines. Match the
first key in the original 40-entry order, conjugate its first matching suffix,
rotate only that key's replies, and handle consecutive repeated word lists with
a separate cyclic queue. Preserve trailing-I conjugation, fallback replies,
capitalization, spelling and the two newlines after each response.

Each iteration i starts from the original initial state and selects the first
(i mod 20) input lines. It recomputes the conversation and consumes its complete
character length. The driver checks every length against the reviewed 20-entry
reference cycle and reports iterations:sum:checked. Reference lengths are
checker data, never substituted for computing a conversation.

## History, revision, authorship and aliases

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/eliza/Main.hs,
Makefile, eliza.stdin and the three stdout fixtures. The header credits the Hugs
version to Mark P. Jones, January 12, 1992, adapted from a Pascal implementation
provided by James Risner with original Pascal code apparently by Robert
Migliaccio. Retain that wording rather than resolving uncertain attribution.
The selected program and 335-byte conversation state no separate redistribution
notice or dataset author; no notice from an unrelated component is substituted.
The exact input is retained, not regenerated or replaced with invented dialogue.

The explicit eliza-lazy/strict names identify evaluation variants of this nofib
implementation. They do not claim to reproduce every historical ELIZA script.

## Lazy and strict variants

Reply queues use explicit shared, memoized cycles in both variants. The initial
state is shared across sessions, as in the Haskell top-level value. A session
constructs a persistent new key table and advances queue pointers without
mutating the initial response positions. Memoized queue nodes may be reused;
computed conversations and their lengths are not cached across iterations.

The lazy variant memoizes candidate-reply and output-character spines, demanding
the first candidate only. Response and next-state fields have separate memoized
delays, avoiding construction of an unused final key table. A fixed response does not force its unused conjugated
suffix. The strict variant constructs finite candidate lists, conjugations and
output characters eagerly. Cyclic queues remain lazy to avoid turning an
infinite producer into a divergent strict initialization. Full output agrees;
allocation, retention and the timing of unused candidate work can differ.

## Portable SML97 translation

Response keys/templates, repeated replies and conjugations are extracted with
an export-only Haskell observer, with all source text retained. SML strings store
words/templates; input lines and word lists are finite strict lists. Loading the
fixed file replaces lazy getContents/lines. Only each selected prefix is trimmed
and tokenized, but loading the small file is strict and happens once per run.
String case conversion and conjugation materialize strings, whereas Haskell
strings are lazy character lists. Output characters and candidate spines retain
explicit delays where evaluation differs between the named variants.

The composed tails/filter/map pipeline is represented by a delayed candidate
list with the same nonempty tails, key order and first-match behavior; intermediate
list layers are fused in this translation. Uppercase mapping within a candidate
uses a finite strict word list. Record these representation and allocation
changes when interpreting measurements; this is not an assertion of identical
Haskell allocation. Reconstructing key tables and rotating cyclic queues preserve
the original persistent state algorithm rather than using mutable keyword counters.

Source numeric parameters and lengths fit signed 31-bit Int. The summary uses
IntInf accumulation explicitly. The initial key-table spine and word preparation use strict finite lists.
Input is ASCII; character behavior outside the
retained workload is not claimed to implement Haskell's full Unicode semantics.
The SML driver checks its positive repetition bound of 65000. It replaces many
printed length lines with checked aggregation; I/O and result checking are
included costs. No external library, runtime extension or compiler hint is needed.

## Profiles and diagnostic questions

Smoke uses 20 iterations to cover one complete prefix cycle. Normal preserves
NORM 13000 and selected large preserves SLOW 65000. FAST 1300 is also checked with
the unmodified original and its fixture. Every run recomputes all selected
sessions, including repeated occurrences of a prefix. No universal size argument
is imposed on conversation data. Default profile time/memory limits apply.

Source-based diagnostic questions concern ordered keyword matching, repeated
case conversion, candidate demand, persistent key-table copying, shared cyclic
queues, character streams and strict finite-result retention. These are
hypotheses until supported by measurements. Standard compiler reports compare
identical SML; original Haskell runs supply correctness evidence.

## References and validation

Unmodified original outputs agree with all three upstream fixtures. An
independent ordered-key/counter model agrees with all 20 complete conversation
prefixes and all 65000 original length rows. Export-only observers supply exact
full response bytes, including punctuation and blank lines. Additional complete
sessions cover repeated inputs, key rotation, trailing I, empty suffix defaults,
fallback and punctuation. SML checks include both variants' full output, cyclic
sharing, demanded/unused suffixes and wrong/truncated/extra output rejection.
Broader host/profile validation is claimed only where recorded in the results.

Joseph Weizenbaum, [ELIZA—A Computer Program for the Study of Natural Language
Communication Between Man and Machine](https://doi.org/10.1145/365153.365168),
Communications of the ACM 9(1), 1966, pp.36–45, provides historical context for
keyword-based conversational programs. It is not a specification for the
particular Hugs response table or evidence of current compiler performance.
The retained nofib source supplies that implementation's exact behavior; the
suite's nofib and measurement survey supplies comparison methodology.

[Complete provenance](eliza-lazy/PROVENANCE.md).

## eliza-strict

Selected finite candidate/output evaluation: strict; cyclic reply queues remain memoized.

## Algorithm and workload

Run the source's ordered keyword/tail search and cyclic response selection over
its fixed conversation. Trim only space, period, exclamation mark, question mark
and comma from line ends; split into words and discard empty lines. Match the
first key in the original 40-entry order, conjugate its first matching suffix,
rotate only that key's replies, and handle consecutive repeated word lists with
a separate cyclic queue. Preserve trailing-I conjugation, fallback replies,
capitalization, spelling and the two newlines after each response.

Each iteration i starts from the original initial state and selects the first
(i mod 20) input lines. It recomputes the conversation and consumes its complete
character length. The driver checks every length against the reviewed 20-entry
reference cycle and reports iterations:sum:checked. Reference lengths are
checker data, never substituted for computing a conversation.

## History, revision, authorship and aliases

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/eliza/Main.hs,
Makefile, eliza.stdin and the three stdout fixtures. The header credits the Hugs
version to Mark P. Jones, January 12, 1992, adapted from a Pascal implementation
provided by James Risner with original Pascal code apparently by Robert
Migliaccio. Retain that wording rather than resolving uncertain attribution.
The selected program and 335-byte conversation state no separate redistribution
notice or dataset author; no notice from an unrelated component is substituted.
The exact input is retained, not regenerated or replaced with invented dialogue.

The explicit eliza-lazy/strict names identify evaluation variants of this nofib
implementation. They do not claim to reproduce every historical ELIZA script.

## Lazy and strict variants

Reply queues use explicit shared, memoized cycles in both variants. The initial
state is shared across sessions, as in the Haskell top-level value. A session
constructs a persistent new key table and advances queue pointers without
mutating the initial response positions. Memoized queue nodes may be reused;
computed conversations and their lengths are not cached across iterations.

The lazy variant memoizes candidate-reply and output-character spines, demanding
the first candidate only. Response and next-state fields have separate memoized
delays, avoiding construction of an unused final key table. A fixed response does not force its unused conjugated
suffix. The strict variant constructs finite candidate lists, conjugations and
output characters eagerly. Cyclic queues remain lazy to avoid turning an
infinite producer into a divergent strict initialization. Full output agrees;
allocation, retention and the timing of unused candidate work can differ.

## knucleotide3-64

Selected key threshold: 31; fixed 64-bit source-bit representation.

## Algorithm and workload

Extract the THREE record from FASTA, encode A/T/C/G as 0/1/2/3, and count packed
keys in persistent-across-pass chained hash tables. Print sorted one-/two-base
frequencies and the five original query counts. Preserve the loop's omitted last
window and the absence of clearing between lengths: leading-zero keys of different
lengths can alias. These are source behavior, not errors for this port to fix.
The driver validates every output byte and EOF before reporting its byte count.

## History, upstream revision and notices

Sandmark 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507,
benchmarks/benchmarksgame/knucleotide3.ml. Its header credits Troestler Christophe,
Mauricio Fernandez, Fabrice Le Fessant, Roman Kashitsyn and KC Sivaramakrishnan,
whose change removes parallelization. Retain that header, directory Revised BSD
notice, aggregate Unlicense, README, Dune and fasta3 input-generator source.

Portable buffer/table support follows OCaml 4.14.1, pinned at
99cb5d93fc30f1a6f3e69f5aa5d2063994d33a93. Selected hashtbl.ml/buffer.ml bytes match
the installed sources. Retain the Xavier Leroy/INRIA copyrights, LGPL 2.1 notice
and linking exception, including the notice in the SML adaptation. Generated
FASTA carries the same fasta3 provenance as the other nucleotide imports; no
unattributed external dataset is added.

## Numeric variants and source differences

knucleotide3-64 preserves threshold 31: all current query lengths use single packed
keys. knucleotide3-32 preserves threshold 15: the 18-base query uses two packed
components in a separate table. Both tables are allocated in both variants,
including an unused second table in the64 variant. Pair hashing uses only the
first component, with equality comparing both. These materially different key/
table representations merit separate names. Both run identically on all SML
host widths using explicit Word64 rather than native Int width selection.

The byte-key knucleotide benchmark clears its table per length and counts the
last window. It is a separate algorithm/representation variant; its fixtures
are not interchangeable with the packed counter. Do not consolidate them.

## Portable SML97 translation

Multiply/add and shifts use Word64. Source32 components need at most 30 significant
bits; 64-bit source packed keys need at most 62, with 36 used by the largest current
query. No wrap occurs in the selected positive domain. Explicit Small/Large
constructors select the key representation; SML tagging/Word64 boxing may add
indirections compared with native OCaml ints/pairs. Counts, bucket indices and
profile sizes fit signed 31-bit Int. This is not a claim that host-native integer
arithmetic has the same allocation cost.

A mutable chained table keeps source initial capacity 262144, identity/first-key
hashes, head insertion and doubling above two entries per bucket. Transfer
preserves collision-chain order. Lookup uses an option instead of Not_found;
that library boundary and its allocation/branch cost are explicit adaptations.
The table is never cleared between the seven count passes. Both table instances
and sequence buffers are recreated per Benchmark.run, preventing a repeated
in-process invocation from accumulating results from its previous invocation.

The portable input buffer begins at 1000 and doubles as needed, following the
same copied-buffer algorithm used by the existing byte-key port. This replaces
the source's fixed 130000000-byte initial reservation for its much larger default
input; record the changed allocation footprint when comparing profiles. Per-line
encoding preserves ASCII tab values, including the source's default0 for unknown
bytes. Initial comment/catch-all handling, prefix header selection, later empty-
line failure, terminal-LF removal and stopping at the next record remain.

Portable merge sort replaces OCaml List.sort while preserving descending
binary64 frequencies and lexical ties. Binary64 operation association and three-
decimal formatting remain. The original hardcoded filename becomes an argument;
complete output checking replaces stdout and is included measured work. No FFI,
effect handler, parallel feature or prerequisite runtime change is introduced.

## Inputs, profiles and diagnostic questions

Smoke/normal/large reuse the pinned fasta3 inputs with n=1000/50000/500000,
seed 42 and width 60. THREE contains 5000/250000/2500000 bases. The original Dune
n=25000000 and auxiliary n=5000000 remain documented, not claimed executed here.
Large is an explicitly reduced scaling input. Input generation is available in
the suite's portable SML fasta3 implementation, with exact complete files pinned.
Default profile limits apply; original outputs for all selected sizes are retained.

Source-based questions concern packed-key arithmetic, width-dependent pair
allocation, repeated packing, cumulative aliasing, identity-hash collisions,
retained tables, bucket growth, buffer copying and string formatting. They remain
hypotheses until supported by inspection or measurements. Standard reports use
identical SML; OCaml supplies correctness references.

## Reference evidence and validation

The unmodified64-bit OCaml program agrees with an independent packed-key model on
all complete smoke/normal/large outputs. A separate observer changes only the
threshold to 15 and agrees with the independent two-table/pair model. It does not
constitute execution by a 32-bit OCaml compiler. Managed32-bit SML host results are
recorded separately. Model statistics retain every pass's entries and total counts.

Original complete edge fixtures cover case conversion, THREE-prefix matching,
initial comments, next-record termination, no final LF, short/empty input and
unknown bytes. The original library observer records 512 deliberately colliding
keys through repeated resize, exact fold traversal and every smoke pass's table
statistics. Tests cover omitted-window bounds, cumulative leading-zero aliases,
31-/15-digit representations, pair hashing, both full output variants, and
wrong/truncated/extra output rejection. Large SML and additional host validation
are claimed only where recorded. Retained program/library sources explain the
exact algorithm; the suite's measurement survey supplies methodological context.

[Complete provenance](knucleotide3-64/PROVENANCE.md).

## infer-lazy

Selected value evaluation: lazy; parser/result spines remain memoized.

## Algorithm and workload

Parse lambda/let expressions using the source's nondeterministic parser
combinators and greedy cuts. Infer polymorphic types with association-list
environments/substitutions, occurs checks, fresh variables and generalisation/
specialisation. Render the original environment, terms, types, failures and
prompts, and consume every character with the source polynomial hash.

Each of the source's 200 repetitions parses and infers all 16 input lines again.
The fresh-variable counter and substitution reset for every expression. The
initial environment/header are immutable shared setup. Source inputs include
successful inference, malformed syntax, unbound variables and occurs-check
failures; those rejected terms are part of a correct benchmark result.

## History, revision, authorship and aliases

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, real/infer/Main.hs and its
portable Parse, Shows, Term, Type, Environment, FiniteMap, Substitution, Infer,
InferMonad, StateX, MaybeM and MyList support. Preserve local NofibUtils, other
source members, build metadata and all FAST/NORM/SLOW input/output fixtures.
Makefile excludes TestType/TestTerm as separate support tests; the runnable
application is Main.hs. The selected program/data headers state no individual
author or separate redistribution notice. Record that absence without assigning
a grant or attribution from an unrelated component.

Names infer-lazy/strict identify evaluation variants of this application.
They are distinct from the smaller classic/nofib type-inference kernels and
retain the full parsing, polymorphism, state and rendering workload.

## Source details and evaluation variants

Parser alternatives concatenate in source order. starP/plusP retain cutP's first
result and greedy non-backtracking behavior. Its irrefutable result head and
separately delayed value/rest fields share one producer result. Both variants
memoize parser/result-list spines so cut pruning remains effective. The lazy
variant memoizes value fields and term/type constructors as well; the strict
variant evaluates those values eagerly along demanded spines. Input identifiers
use SML strings, and finite input loading/line splitting are strict in both.

Finite-map extension prepends without removing shadowed bindings. Environment
free-variable collection still sees those entries; substitution composition
retains duplicate domain entries and maps old values through one shared new
binding. Preserve first-match lookup, fresh-variable order, syntactic occurs
checks, constructor-name short circuiting and one-occurrence list subtraction.
Unequal constructor arities retain the source's partial-operation behavior.
Rejected inference returns the original failure text; unused error fallbacks
remain deferred in both variants.

## Portable SML97 translation

SML functors express the parser and kernel; explicit memoized delays preserve
sharing. The source's nested StateX/Sub/Counter/Maybe machinery becomes curried
state functions returning an option with the same value/substitution/counter
order. Administrative wrappers are fused, while association lists, substitution
composition, fresh names and update order remain. It is a translation of these
modules, rather than a replacement by mutable union-find inference.

Recursive display functions emit delayed characters with the original precedence,
spaces, parentheses and prompts. ASCII profiles retain exact character behavior;
Unicode outside the retained input domain is not claimed equivalent to Haskell.
Source counters and list sizes fit signed 31-bit Int. The source GHC 64-bit hash
uses explicit Word64 multiply/add wrapping, with its signed result checked via
the equivalent unsigned bit pattern on every SML host width.

Reading the fixed input file anew for each repetition replaces NOINLINE salt
with a portable opaque I/O dependency. This adds input loading costs and prevents
reusing previous inference results as repeated-run answers. The reference file
is also consumed anew. Every rendered byte/EOF and the independent expected
hash are checked before aggregating repetitions:bytes:checked instead of
printing 200 signed hash lines. Checking and I/O are included measured work.
No compiler/runtime extension, FFI or parallel feature is required.

## Profiles and diagnostic questions

Smoke, normal and selected large retain the exact FAST/NORM/SLOW files and all
200 repetitions. Each has 16 lines, with 348/693/1108 bytes; they vary the final
polymorphic-identity application chain. Complete rendered outputs contain
643/990/1404 bytes. Source parse/type failures remain in each input profile.
Default time/memory limits apply. Repetitions are bounded to 1..200 in the driver;
normal profiles do not reuse parsed terms or inferred types across repetitions.

Diagnostic questions concern parser closures/cuts, value demand, association-list
search, shadowed entries, substitution sharing/composition, generalisation,
intermediate type lifetimes, character streams, Word64 hashing and checking.
These are source-based hypotheses until supported by measurements. Standard
reports compare identical SML; Haskell supplies correctness references.

## References and validation

The unmodified original reproduces all three 200-line upstream stdout fixtures.
Export-only observers retain complete rendered texts; an independent polynomial
hash reproduces every original signed result. A separate parser/Algorithm W
model agrees on all 48 profile expressions, comparing types modulo variable
renaming and checking parse/type rejection. It supplements exact source-output
comparisons without specifying every source-parser quirk.

Twenty-four additional original full expression sessions cover parsing, shadowing,
polymorphic let, repeated application, occurs checks and literal let-prefix
behavior. Original boundary observations pin greedy cuts, substitution domain
order/duplicates and shadowed environment variables. Tests compare both full
outputs and check cut demand/sharing, constructor short circuiting, occurs checks,
source partial arity behavior, line splitting and changed/truncated/extra output
or hash rejection. Current bounded Rune preflights reproduce all three complete
texts and both full 200-iteration normal computations. Other validation is claimed
only where recorded.

Luis Damas and Robin Milner, [Principal type-schemes for functional programs](https://doi.org/10.1145/582153.582176),
POPL 1982, pp. 207–212, supplies context for polymorphic let inference. The retained
modules specify this particular implementation and its parser/data behavior;
the paper does not establish current compiler rankings. The suite's nofib and
measurement survey supplies experimental context.

[Complete provenance](infer-lazy/PROVENANCE.md).

hash reproduces every original signed result. A separate parser/Algorithm W
model agrees on all 48 profile expressions, comparing types modulo variable
renaming and checking parse/type rejection. It supplements exact source-output
comparisons without specifying every source-parser quirk.

Twenty-four additional original full expression sessions cover parsing, shadowing,
polymorphic let, repeated application, occurs checks and literal let-prefix
behavior. Original boundary observations pin greedy cuts, substitution domain
order/duplicates and shadowed environment variables. Tests compare both full
outputs and check cut demand/sharing, constructor short circuiting, occurs checks,
source partial arity behavior, line splitting and changed/truncated/extra output
or hash rejection. Current bounded Rune preflights reproduce all three complete
texts and both full 200-iteration normal computations. Other validation is claimed
only where recorded.

Luis Damas and Robin Milner, [Principal type-schemes for functional programs](https://doi.org/10.1145/582153.582176),
POPL 1982, pp. 207–212, supplies context for polymorphic let inference. The retained
modules specify this particular implementation and its parser/data behavior;
the paper does not establish current compiler rankings. The suite's nofib and
measurement survey supplies experimental context.

[Complete provenance](infer-strict/PROVENANCE.md).

## cichelli-lazy

Selected count/candidate evaluation: lazy; search-result spines remain memoized.

## Algorithm and workload

Search for character weights whose word hash is length + weight(first) +
weight(last). Assign previously unknown end characters in lexicographic order,
reject duplicate hashes and partial ranges wider than 22, and stop at the first
complete solution. Preserve persistent character associations, optional range
bounds and list-based used hashes. Feedback counts terminal leaves, not all
recursive states. Emit every original status/count/witness byte without adding
line separators.

The source loops over indices 1..n. Even indices search the original 22 keywords;
odd indices append a duplicate first keyword. blocked brings determined keys
forward while preserving partition order. The duplicate makes odd searches fail
with 324 leaves; even searches succeed with 113994 leaves. The successful 17-letter
assignment maps all 22 words to the contiguous interval 4..25.

## History, revision, authorship and aliases

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/cichelli/Main.hs,
Prog.hs, Auxil.hs, Key.lhs, Interval.hs, Makefile and stdout fixtures. Prog labels
its implementation strictly serial search; the unused Interval constants do not
introduce polling, parallelism or a stopping threshold. Preserve the complete
literate Key file, including inactive alternative datasets, while importing only
its active 22-key definition. Comments include partain adaptation markers; they
state no full program author or separate redistribution notice. No grant or
attribution from another component is substituted.

Names cichelli-lazy/strict preserve meaningful evaluation variants of this nofib
program. The historical algorithm name is retained without attributing this
particular Haskell implementation to the paper's author.

## Exact source behavior and evaluation variants

freqsorted is the active identity function; its commented frequency sort remains
disabled. Histogram/right-fold order and maximum 17 distinct end characters are
retained. Candidate weights include both endpoints 0..17. The range bound stays 22,
even for correctness calls on key prefixes. union tests both new end characters
against the original left list, preserving duplicate characters when appropriate.
Associations prepend new bindings; successful witness order is unchanged.

Both variants memoize candidate-result/control spines and keep firstSuccess's
short circuiting. The lazy variant memoizes arithmetic feedback fields and
constructs candidate arguments on demand. Strict evaluation materializes finite
candidate argument lists and combines counts eagerly. Unvisited result searches
remain unexecuted in both. The source's association lists, range pruning, visited
leaf counts, first solution and output agree; allocation/retention differ.

## Portable SML97 translation

SML keeps the immutable key/hash-set/association representations and source
right-fold histogram/partition algorithms. Attributed-key and blocked-key
preparation use strict finite lists in both variants; the source's lazy library
spines are not reproduced throughout this small setup. Mutable memoization
supports demand-sensitive search/result/count cells. No alternative perfect-hash
construction, bitset occupancy kernel or mutable character table replaces the
source algorithm. The independent reference model uses a set for a separate
correctness implementation.

All selected indices, weights, hashes and counts fit signed 31-bit Int. Hashes
are at most 43. Counts are nonnegative sums of visited leaves; every intermediate
sum is bounded by the recorded final 113994 maximum for these fixed problems.
Native Int therefore preserves the source 64-bit arithmetic on this domain.
No arbitrary-precision or modular arithmetic is silently introduced.

A fixed SML-generated index file replaces the implicit loop with an opaque input
dependency: first n, then the exact source indices 1..n. Each index invokes a fresh
search, with no previous parity result reused. Input parsing/checking adds driver
cost. The driver consumes complete status/witness text and validates every byte
and EOF before reporting n:bytes:checked. It bounds n to 0..300 and indices to 1..300.
Immutable key/frequency setup may be shared, lifted or exported by a compiler;
input-dependent searches occur inside Benchmark.run.

## Profiles and diagnostic questions

Smoke retains FAST 6, normal NORM 60, and selected large SLOW 300. Inputs alternate
odd failures and even successes in source order. Complete outputs have
507/5070/25350 bytes. Large increases repetitions of the same fixed key problems,
preserving the original profile rather than inventing a larger dictionary.
There is no separately acquired dataset or random seed. Default resource limits
apply. Input generation, kernel and checking remain portable SML97.

Source-based questions concern higher-order search, pruning, repeated association
lookup, count thunks, candidate construction, persistent data lifetimes and
immutable setup placement. They remain hypotheses until supported by analysis
or measurements. Standard reports compare identical SML; Haskell is a correctness
reference. Counters/instrumentation stay separate from headline timings.

## References and validation

The unmodified original agrees with all three complete stdout fixtures. Export-
only observers record exact data/histogram/block order, both parity statuses and
key-prefix 0/1/2/5/10/15/22 results. An independent set-based search agrees on all
leaf counts, first witnesses and profile outputs; it visits 116083 states for the
full even search and 631 for the odd failure. These state counts are distinct
from source feedback leaf counts.

Both SML variants reproduce the exact parity outputs and full 60-run normal
profile in bounded Rune preflights. Semantic tests cover all source prefixes,
full witnesses, histogram/block order, original union behavior, range pruning,
first-success demand, count sharing and changed/truncated/extra output rejection.
Broader or large SML validation is claimed only where recorded.

Richard J. Cichelli, [Minimal perfect hash functions made simple](https://doi.org/10.1145/358808.358813),
Communications of the ACM 23(1), January 1980, pp. 17–19, provides historical context.
The DOI registration metadata is retained. The exact nofib modules specify this
variant's ordering, disabled sorting and counters; the paper is not evidence of
current compiler performance. The suite's nofib/measurement survey supplies
experimental context.

[Complete provenance](cichelli-lazy/PROVENANCE.md).

## scs-lazy

Selected approximate numerical payload evaluation: lazy.

## Algorithm and workload

Parse the original inverter circuit and SI-valued parameters. Build exact
rational circuit/derivative matrices, run the source Gauss–Jordan reductions and
null-space corrections, then convert the prepared operators to binary64.
Integrate rational time and approximate circuit state, update sources, solve and
correct constraints, and evaluate tunnelling events with the original seeded
combined generator and energy/probability formulas. Each tick emits its base
output and, when selected, one corrected post-event output at the same time.
The next tick integrates the last state. End-time selection is inclusive.

The port formats every time/vector value and counts quoted-string escapes,
retaining the original Main's length(show output) consumer work. It also validates
all numerical results against complete reference traces before returning a stable
rows:points:checked summary. Numerical validation is stronger than the upstream
Done-only stdout fixture.

## History, revision, authorship and notices

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, real/scs/Main.hs, Types,
Parse, ParseLib, RandomFix, LinearAlgebra, Simulate, Makefile, scs.stdout and
runtime_files/inverter.in. The contribution email retained in Makefile credits
Erik van der Meer's masters-thesis prototype, sent 17 March 2000. It explains exact
rational preprocessing, approximate simulation and the inverter/temperature choice.
Selected program/data state no separate redistribution notice; individual circuit
authorship is unstated. Preserve all original text without assigning a grant from
another component.

RandomFix credits Lennart Augustsson's transliteration, Alastair Reid's 1997 changes
and Erik van der Meer's 1999 Hugs 1.4 adaptation. Its range mapper differs from the
later System.Random 1.1 implementation elsewhere in this suite. Retain its own
source/history. Primary GHC base sources are pinned at
00920f176b0235d5bb52a8e054d89a664f8938fe, with University of Glasgow and other
notices preserved in the full base/LICENSE. Reference array 0.5.4.0 is pinned at
77990b2132ba688f6282822891da2b9455e33c2f with its separate notice.

## Algorithms, demand and variants

Keep exact rational ranks/pivots and the first maximum-magnitude pivot on ties.
Matrix updates are persistent; ordered accumulation retains source r,t,c and r,c
contribution order. Conditional preprocessing remains memoized: an algebraically
invertible circuit avoids the unused empty third reduction. Float conversion
uses exact integer division and nearest-even rounding before power-of-two scaling,
including separately tested subnormal/overflow boundaries.

RandomFix keeps arbitrary-precision seed/range arithmetic, original base 2147483561,
iLogBase draw count and fold-right digit accumulation. Word32 expresses its
representable signed 32-bit Schrage transitions on every SML host. Result heads
and state transitions have separate shared delays, preserving skipped heads and
array overrides. Each tick advances size random values for offsets and one event
selection position. Candidate events, correction/energy calculations, negative
probability clamping, total normalization, cumulative order and strict p<cdf
selection remain. The selected post-event solve/correction is recomputed as written.

scs-lazy memoizes numerical array cells. scs-strict forces approximate matrices
and newly constructed numerical vectors, including finite normalized probability
values. Parser, rational preprocessing conditions, random streams and trace
spines remain memoized in both. The strict scope is numerical payloads, preserving
finite termination and source control pruning. No previous trajectory is reused
as a repeated-run answer.

## Portable SML97 translation

Memoized cell vectors replace boxed immutable Data.Array payloads. Mutable arrays
are confined to construction/update before freezing cell pointers; numeric values
remain immutable. Ordered update callbacks avoid intermediate association-list
spines while retaining scalar operation order. Gaussian arithmetic follows pinned
GHC.Real cross-product/reduce operations and exact IntInf ratios; approximate
operators use binary64. GHC.List's strict left sum is preserved. Native Int indices,
row/point counters and formatted lengths fit signed 31-bit for selected profiles.

The source parser's nondeterministic alternatives, allow-null repetition,
whitespace/SI conventions and singleton complete-parse check remain. Existing
portable parser primitives are shared; greedy cut repetition from infer is not
used. Identifiers/input text use finite SML strings and lists over the selected
ASCII domain. Source filename stems become explicit .in paths. Reading and parsing
input occur per Benchmark.run, followed by fresh preprocessing/simulation.

SML GEN17 formatting replaces Haskell's shortest Double renderer; streamed
formatting/escape counting replaces materializing the whole shown string. The
checked summary omits renderer-dependent lengths. Numerical checking and reference
I/O are included costs. These representation/library/output changes belong in
interpretation of comparisons. No FFI, parallelism, effect handler or prerequisite
compiler/runtime feature is introduced.

## Inputs, validation and resource profiles

Smoke preserves inverter, seed 345, dt 10n, end 2u, temperature 1 and background 0.
Normal preserves dt 2n/end 4u; selected large preserves dt 400p/end 4u, with other
parameters identical. The source's omitted optional background is explicitly 0.
The literal pinned circuit is retained. Its 18 variables produce 371/2913/11315
rows, including 170/912/1314 extra event outputs. Large refines the time grid.
Inputs/matrices/time use exact ratios; source-step/profile parameters are not
replaced by a universal size argument. Default resource limits apply.

Every reference label, dimension, rational time, row count and EOF must agree.
Each finite current/voltage value is checked with relative bound 1e-11 and absolute
floors 1e-24 amperes/1e-15 volts respectively. Floors cover cancellation near zero;
relative bounds permit binary64 rounding differences. They validate this fixed
workload, not physical accuracy. Perturbed inside/outside values, changed labels,
times/values, nonfinite values, dimensions and truncated/extra traces are tested.
Event times and row counts are checked exactly alongside numerical bounds.

Original and independent rational/float implementations agree exactly on all
three full traces and prepared matrices. The independent minimum distance from
selection draws to cumulative thresholds is .00187519 for smoke and greater than
8.56e-6 for normal/large. Explicit event/time checks still apply independently of
that observed margin. All 3960 rounding-boundary/preprocessing bit cases agree on
Rune. Small original runs and generated RC/RL/conductor-current test circuits
exercise all element classes, zero temperature, background charge and huge seeds.
Synthetic circuits are test data, not upstream workload profiles.

## Host observations and references

The auxiliary bit encoder converts an already integral significand using
truncation. Separate nearest-conversion probes retain Poly/ML 5.9.2 failures; a
local report records this native Basis defect. Three SML/NJ variants reproduce
the existing fromManExp subnormal report outside the workload's normal/zero
conversion domain. Legacy 64-bit numerical replays also vary under default allocation;
a separate 64 MiB nursery replay passes. Default settings/expected values remain
unchanged, failures are retained and incorrect results cannot contribute timings.
These are recorded host observations, not kernel patches or an upstream-fix claim.

The unmodified GHC 9.4.7 program reproduces all Done fixtures. Export-only observers
retain full traces, exact preprocessing, numeric bit patterns, parsing and RNG
vectors. A separate Fraction/mutable-matrix/binary64 simulator agrees exactly on
all profiles. Broader host and large SML claims remain limited to recorded checks.

P. L'Ecuyer, [Efficient and portable combined random number generators](https://doi.org/10.1145/62959.62969),
Communications of the ACM 31(6), June 1988, pp. 742–751, supplies the source-cited
generator context. The retained 2000 contribution email and exact modules specify
this simulator; pinned GHC numeric/array sources explain its library operations.
The suite's methodology survey frames measurements without transferring historical
performance claims to current SML compilers.

[Complete provenance](scs-lazy/PROVENANCE.md).

## listcompr-lazy

Selected AST evaluation: lazy. Consumer: count rendered character spine.

### Algorithm and workload

Compile the fixed five-definition program containing list comprehensions into
applications and local recursive helper definitions, then render the result.
Each input repetition translates the original definitions again. The consumer
counts the rendered character list's spine without demanding character heads.
It computes the actual output length; 626*n is only the reviewed result check.
Full rendered texts are checked separately on small inputs.

### History, authorship and aliases

The source is nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798,
`spectral/hartel/listcompr/Main.hs` and `listcopy/Main.hs`, their Makefiles,
stdout fixtures and `spectral/hartel/Fast2haskell.hs`. Both complete sources and
the shared shim are preserved below upstream/. The collection name associates
these programs with Hartel; these files state no full individual authorship or
separate redistribution notice. No grant is inferred from another benchmark.
The original program labels remain in the suite names, with explicit evaluation
suffixes. The source core agrees byte for byte after removing the reviewed
benchmark label, copy wrapper and unused line-counter wrapper; the archive
records the normalization and source identities. They share the SML compiler
kernel while retaining their materially different consumer pipelines.

### Known variants and source semantics

listcompr counts the rendered stream directly. listcopy first recursively copies
its spine, retaining the same character cells. It does not reuse the original
spine, duplicate the input program, or force each character. Source `f_tp` maps
`f_td`; the nearby lambda-lifting helpers are unreachable from this workload.
Comprehension generators introduce parent-name-derived local functions; inner
let definitions retain the enclosing top-level name during transformation.
The renderer drops only the first semicolon from its `;\n` prefix, retaining
the newline. Nonalphabetic application names print the first two arguments and
ignore further arguments. The translation preserves these source quirks.

The lazy variant memoizes expression payloads and AST/list spines. The strict
variant materializes those finite AST values and spines eagerly. Both keep names,
rendered character heads/spines and the copy consumer memoized, because the source
length consumer must not demand unused characters. Fixed constructor argument
lists and the five-definition input setup use finite SML lists; their payloads
follow the selected evaluation policy. This setup translation does not attempt
to reproduce every Haskell list-library thunk. The selected program demands its
constructor argument spines; additional malformed/demand-sensitive examples are

## wang-lazy

Selected numerical and list evaluation: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Apply the source's blocked elimination pipeline to a fixed tridiagonal numerical
problem, render every solution value, and compute an ASCII-sum/length checksum.
The input is n blocks of n+1 rows: boundary coefficients (0,3,2,5) and (2,3,0,5),
with (2,3,2,7) in between. Preserve forward elimination, reverse corrections,
coarse boundary equations and reconstruction. The middle input block is shared
across its n-2 uses. Every repetition constructs and solves a fresh problem.

### History, authorship, revision and aliases

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798,
`spectral/hartel/wang/Main.hs`, Makefile, its three 500-line stdout fixtures and
`spectral/hartel/Fast2haskell.hs`. Complete bytes are preserved under upstream/.
The collection name records the Hartel association; these files state no full
individual authorship or separate redistribution notice. No attribution or grant
is inferred from another component or from the short name Wang. This source is
a numerical workload. The established name is preserved with explicit lazy and
strict evaluation suffixes.

### Known variants and exact source behavior

Both variants retain the source equations, tuple fields, sharing, list order and
source operation grouping. The lazy variant memoizes numerical fields, matrix
rows and list spines; the strict variant evaluates these finite values eagerly.
Rendering remains a memoized character stream in both. Strict evaluation can
calculate fields that the lazy consumer leaves unused. Fast2haskell's miraseq is
identity on its second argument and does not force its first.

The source el31/el3 reconstruction expressions divide the diagonal by the
computed residual. Their empty-row cases divide the anchor RHS by its diagonal.
The source f_dist pairs the first boundary with the first matrix2 block, while
the leading output also uses that block. Preserve both choices exactly. Small
nonuniform inputs distinguish these source recurrences and pairing from other
reconstructions; the uniform all-ones workload alone cannot establish this
translation detail. Nearby example matrices and generic Fast library helpers
are unreachable from the benchmark entrypoint and are retained in source only.

### Portable SML97 translation and adaptations

Use the original four-field real tuples and persistent list structure, with
explicit memoized numerical cells for the lazy evaluation policy. Scalar factors
shared by several fields remain shared cells. The unused input/block fields are
not replaced with a precomputed solution. Source numeric operations and grouped
subtractions retain their order. The fixed generator is SML97; shell code only
handles compilation, processes and operating-system limits.

The selected arithmetic uses binary64 real values. Each computed scalar must be
finite and within absolute 1e-10 of one, substantially above the original trace's
maximum observed 5.38e-13 error while rejecting perturbations hidden by the
source formatter's 0.0005 threshold. The tighter check is additional validation;
the original threshold and ASCII rendering remain in the consumer. All selected
validated values render as 1. The decimal fallback is outside accepted profiles.
Complete reference comparisons also cover nonuniform values, independently of
this fixed-input bound.

Checksum accumulation uses strict SML integers. The source traverses all rendered
characters and computes sum(ord chars)+length, followed by /length. Per-invocation
checksums fit signed 31-bit Int: at n=150 the result is 2181430/45750. The driver
validates every generated checksum against the reviewed all-ones text calculation,
formats each repetition's result, consumes its emitted byte count, and reports
repetitions:checksum:bytes. This replaces 500 separate output writes with controlled
suite output while retaining numerical generation, character traversal and integer
formatting. The byte count is at most 7000 for the selected profiles. No sum of
500 large checksums is held in a narrow integer.

### Compiler/runtime questions

Investigate the effects of delayed real fields, shared blocks and elimination
factors, eager intermediate tuples, list traversal, allocation and collector
retention. These are source-derived hypotheses, separate from measured findings.
The original GHC program supplies correctness references. Measurements compare the identical SML program across
compilers. SML/NJ-specific diagnostic failures remain recorded with their default
settings; separate larger-nursery replays do not replace those failures or alter
the kernel. Causes remain unreduced unless a separate report establishes them.

### Inputs, correctness and references

| Profile | Block size n | Repetitions | One source checksum | Suite result |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| smoke | 25 | 1 | 66805/1375 | 1:66805/1375:11 |
| normal | 80 | 500 | 631490/13200 | 500:631490/13200:6500 |
| large | 150 | 500 | 2181430/45750 | 500:2181430/45750:7000 |

Normal and large retain the source NORM_OPTS/SLOW_OPTS and all 500 entrypoint
repetitions. Smoke preserves FAST_OPTS=25 and reduces only repetitions to one.
Default suite time/memory limits apply. Source dimensions, coefficient values,
block sharing, numeric type, work limit and all output adaptations are explicit.

The unmodified GHC program matches every byte of all three 500-line fixtures.
Full single-invocation observers record 650/6480/22650 values. An independent
mutable blocked solver agrees bit for bit with GHC on those 29780 values and
124 varied values from five nonuniform inputs. The SML semantic checker compares
all values with absolute+relative bounds, checks original checksums, repeat output,
source reconstruction formulas, unused RHS demand, memoized factors and deliberately
perturbed/nonfinite values. Default SML/NJ failures and separate replays are kept
as diagnostics. Whole-program normal and large Rune pilots retain all 500 solves.
Recorded coverage and the full repository check belong in validation.md and
results/m3-wang; these pilot facts alone do not close M3.

[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) provides suite
context. The pinned source supplies the algorithm and evaluation evidence here.
No unverified historical algorithm attribution or general solver claim is made.

124 varied values from five nonuniform inputs. The SML semantic checker compares
all values with absolute+relative bounds, checks original checksums, repeat output,
source reconstruction formulas, unused RHS demand, memoized factors and deliberately
perturbed/nonfinite values. Default SML/NJ failures and separate replays are kept
as diagnostics. Whole-program normal and large Rune pilots retain all 500 solves.
Recorded coverage and the full repository check belong in validation.md and
results/m3-wang; these pilot facts alone do not close M3.

[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) provides suite
context. The pinned source supplies the algorithm and evaluation evidence here.
No unverified historical algorithm attribution or general solver claim is made.


## fft-nofib-lazy

Selected collection/value evaluation: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Run both original transforms on a real ramp [63,62,...,0] repeated 2^coarse
times. The first transform uses bit-reversed input and iterative fresh arrays;
the second recursively transforms lists and uses the source join/reorder pass.
Compare every result, render its status character and consume the complete
status stream with the source ASCII-sum/length checksum. Both transforms share
the generated input and its 64 memoized complex payloads.

### History, authorship, revision and aliases

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798,
`spectral/hartel/fft/Main.hs`, Makefile, three 360-line stdout fixtures, and
`spectral/hartel/Fast2haskell.hs`. Preserve their complete bytes under upstream/.
The collection name records the Hartel association; the program/shim files state
no full individual authorship or separate redistribution notice. The related
GHC Complex module has a University of Glasgow 2001 notice and BSD-style license;
its file and base-library license are preserved with their own scope.

The classic SML fft keeps the unsuffixed name. This distinct nofib workload uses
fft-nofib-lazy/strict. It runs two array/list algorithms with a different input
and consumer. genfft generates transform source text; its embedded numerical FFT
helpers are unreachable there. These are distinct workloads with shared ancestry,
not duplicate runnable implementations.

### Evaluation variants and source semantics

GHC 9.4.7 Data.Complex at revision
00920f176b0235d5bb52a8e054d89a664f8938fe declares both components strict. The SML
complex pair therefore has strict binary64 fields in both variants. The lazy
variant memoizes whole complex values, array lookups/indices, comparison strings
and collection spines. The strict variant evaluates these finite values/spines
eagerly. The shared pi value follows the selected evaluation policy. Record
initialization can consequently move between compilation/startup and first use
on different host adapters; headline reports compare identical SML sources.

Both array butterfly outputs share z=root*y and their input lookup cells. The
list transform shares its root per recursive node and shares the product list
between plus/minus branches. Preserve source root arguments, including large
array angles; no modular reduction or twiddle-table substitution changes them.
List reordering retains split/join traversal rather than replacing it with a
direct permutation. Fast2haskell's miraseq does not demand its first argument.

### Portable SML97 translation and adaptations

Fresh SML arrays model the functional Haskell arrays: populate each new array,
then keep it read-only while later stages refer to it. Explicit association lists
and pair order are retained for butterfly stages. Array.tabulate supplies the
shim's tabulation helper; this replaces its library association-building layer.
Standard initialization supplies a shared zero cell. A separate seen array and
write counter validate complete unique index coverage before any stage escapes.
These extra validation allocations and bounds checks are part of the SML workload.
The input and stage arrays, lists, shared cells and arithmetic remain distinct;
there is no in-place butterfly overwrite.

Complex addition/subtraction/multiplication retain the pinned base module's field
expressions and operation grouping. The shim's log2 retains logarithm, rounding
and conversion operations. Nonnegative bounded bit operations use fixed Word32
or div/mod2 equivalents. At 2048 points, index products stay below 2^22 and all
source/driver integers fit signed 31 bits. Standard SML operations replace the
Haskell libraries; no compiler/runtime prerequisite is added.

An independent closed-form spectrum is built once per driver invocation. For
N=64*m and output k, frequencies not divisible by m are zero. For k=m*q,
q=0 gives (2016*m,0); q=1..63 gives (N/2,(N/2)/tan(pi*q/64)). This is the positive
sign, unnormalized transform used by the source. Every scalar from both algorithms
must be finite and within absolute 1e-7 plus relative 1e-12 of that value. The
original method-comparison bound 0.5 also remains. Reference GHC discrepancies
are at most 7.69e-9 (array) and 2.71e-11 (list); an independent direct DFT differs
from the formula by at most 1.21e-8 on the selected inputs. The chosen bound is a
reviewed finite-input rule with margin, not a general floating-point error theorem.
Tests reject perturbations that the original 0.5 comparison would accept.

The original successful t-character stream is retained and consumed; its checksum
is 117*N/N. The driver validates every repeated result, formats the original
checksum/newline contribution and reports repetitions:checksum:emitted-bytes.
Controlled summary output replaces separate per-iteration writes. Invalid
numerical results raise a suite failure before the original verbose difference
formatter. Numerical reference/checking work is included and documented for
SML compiler comparisons.

### Compiler/runtime diagnostic questions

Investigate fresh arrays and persistent lists, array checks, association cells,
complex representation, memoized roots/products, initialization, collector
retention, trigonometric calls and whole-program specialization. These are
source-derived hypotheses until supported by measurements. Count/allocation
instrumentation and serial timings have separate archives. The array algorithm
forms a root per butterfly; the list algorithm shares one per recursive node.
Aggregate results cover both algorithms; they do not isolate either one's cost.

### Profiles, correctness and references

| Profile | Coarse | Points | Repetitions | Suite result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| smoke | 1 | 128 | 1 | 1:14976/128:10 |
| normal | 3 | 512 | 360 | 360:59904/512:3600 |
| large | 5 | 2048 | 360 | 360:239616/2048:4320 |

Normal/large retain original NORM_OPTS/SLOW_OPTS and all 360 iterations. Smoke
preserves FAST_OPTS and reduces only iterations to one. Default limits apply.
The unmodified GHC program agrees with all three 360-line fixtures. Full vectors
from both original algorithms agree with independent direct DFT/analytic checks.
SML tests compare those vectors, nonuniform complex inputs, source checksums,
repeat formatting, bounds, invalid scalars and input sharing. Whole normal
Rune O2 pilots retain all 360 iterations. Other coverage belongs in validation.md.

[Cooley and Tukey](https://www.cs.jhu.edu/~misha/ReadingSeminar/Papers/Cooley65.pdf)
provide algorithmic background; [Partain](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17)
provides nofib context. The pinned sources establish these implementations and
[GHC's Complex definition](https://github.com/ghc/ghc/blob/00920f176b0235d5bb52a8e054d89a664f8938fe/libraries/base/Data/Complex.hs)
establishes field strictness. Source observations, reference discrepancies and
performance hypotheses have the distinct evidence scopes described above.

## genfft-lazy

Selected collection/value evaluation: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Generate source text for unrolled radix-two FFT dependency graphs of sizes
4,8,...,2^(maximum+1). Emit bit-reversed input bindings, every butterfly's
add/subtract/multiply equations, shared root definitions, ordered output groups,
and exact SYNTH/sector text. The measured workload is source generation.
The .program fixtures are data, including the shell-looking header.

### History, authorship, revision and aliases

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798,
`spectral/hartel/genfft/Main.hs`, Makefile, three 300-line stdout fixtures, and
`spectral/hartel/Fast2haskell.hs`. Full original bytes are preserved under upstream/.
The collection name records the Hartel association. These files state no full
individual authorship or separate redistribution notice; none is inferred from
a related module's notice. Keep the established genfft name with explicit lazy
and strict suffixes.

This program shares embedded numerical helpers with Hartel fft, but its entrypoint
only generates text and checks its characters. Those numerical helpers and unused
Fast boilerplate remain in provenance. The numerical FFT and classic SML fft
therefore remain separate workloads.

### Variants and source behavior

The lazy variant memoizes character heads and list spines; the strict variant
constructs those finite lists eagerly. Both preserve input/output name order,
bit reversal, zero-bit insertion, groups of eight output variables, separators,
trailing spaces and final newlines. Shared numeric-name strings remain shared
values when reused. The finite integer bit-list/fold helpers and scalar name
parameters use eager SML operations in both variants; their complete values are
needed by the selected generator. Int.toString replaces the Haskell decimal
formatter on this nonnegative domain. Fast2haskell's miraseq is a no-op.

### Portable SML97 translation and adaptations

Retain the recursive bit-list construction and left fold for insertZero, plus
the source enumeration, map, take/drop, grouping, concatenation and foldr1-style
glue. The latter stays partial on an empty collection and leaves a singleton's
separator unused. The generator constructs source characters for every repetition;
a fixture is used only by the checker. No generated program replaces the kernel.

Indices and shifts are nonnegative and bounded by the selected exponent 8.
Fixed Word32 shifts and div/mod2 implement the source scalar bit operations within
a width-independent domain. Every intermediate integer fits signed 31 bits:
the largest complete output has 426210 ASCII characters and sum+length 31387091.
The driver compares each checksum separately, avoiding a narrow sum of 300 large
checksums. Repeated formatted output has at most 4800 bytes in selected profiles.
There is no reachable floating-point or arbitrary-precision arithmetic.

Load the reviewed complete source fixture once per driver invocation, then compare
every newly generated character for each repetition, including EOF. The source
ASCII-sum/length checksum is also computed and validated. Full byte comparison
rejects a deliberately transposed fixture with the same checksum and length.
This additional checking cost is included in identical-SML compiler comparisons.
The driver formats every iteration's source checksum/newline contribution and
reports repetitions:checksum:emitted-bytes through controlled suite output.

### Compiler/runtime diagnostic questions

Investigate recursive generation, integer/name formatting, sharing, eager/lazy
character lists, concatenation, closure specialization, stack/heap growth and
collector retention. These are source-derived hypotheses until established by
measurement. Byte checking, reference loading, kernel generation and final result
formatting remain visible parts of the SML workload. Profiling/counts remain
separate from headline timings.

### Profiles, correctness and references

| Profile | Maximum exponent | Repetitions | Generated bytes per iteration | Suite result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| smoke | 3 | 1 | 5532 | 1:417707/5532:12 |
| normal | 6 | 300 | 79360 | 300:5925859/79360:4200 |
| large | 8 | 300 | 426210 | 300:31387091/426210:4800 |

Normal/large retain original NORM_OPTS/SLOW_OPTS and all 300 iterations. Smoke
preserves FAST_OPTS and reduces only repetitions to one. Default limits apply.
Every program from exponent one through the maximum is generated in each
iteration. The input parameter is an exponent bound, not a universal size.

Unmodified GHC executions match every byte of all three 300-line fixtures.
Export-only observers record complete source for maxima 0..8. A separate renderer
using bit-mask insertion and reversed binary strings agrees with all selected
bytes. An independent evaluator checks all eight generated dependency graphs
against direct DFTs on nonuniform complex inputs, under documented complex
add/subtract/multiply and positive-unit-root meanings. This validates the graph
model rather than executing the historical target framework.

SML checks compare full source for maxima 0..8 in both modes, repeated output,
wrong/truncated/extra/checksum-colliding fixtures, character sharing, unused
separators and partial empty glue. Whole normal Rune O2 pilots retain all 300
iterations. Recorded host coverage and resource outcomes belong in validation.md.

[Cooley and Tukey](https://www.cs.jhu.edu/~misha/ReadingSeminar/Papers/Cooley65.pdf)
provide algorithmic background and [Partain](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17)
provides suite context. Exact source/history observations and independent graph
checks have their recorded evidence; performance questions remain hypotheses.
