## circsim-lazy

Evaluation: lazy. Consumer: GC show spine only.

### Algorithm and workload

Simulate register circuits through the original immutable processor-state
records, port latches, packet lists and balanced-tree bidirectional scans.
Each clock stores inputs, sends depth-zero messages, evaluates/sends each path
depth, then restores request flags. Routing repeats until requests are acknowledged.
Preserve the register generator and padded processor count. Selected inputs are T.

### History, authorship, revision and aliases

The literate program credits David J. King and John O'Donnell, January 1998.
Its introductory email is dated 2 October 1998 and explicitly calls this sequential
code written with data-parallel combinators. The pin is nofib
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, gc/circsim/Main.lhs and
spectral/circsim/Main.lhs, their Makefiles and spectral stdout fixtures.
Complete source bytes are preserved. The files state no separate redistribution
notice; attribution does not infer a grant. The inventory recognizes the exact
literate authorship heading.

Full source comparison finds only the main consumer/comment different: GC forces
length(show(run ...)) then returns unit; spectral prints the shown trace.
Share the simulator implementation while retaining the inventory names circsim
(GC) and circsim-nofib (spectral), each with lazy/strict evaluation suffixes.
Their head demand and output work differ materially.

### Evaluation variants and source quirks

Signals use a separate F/T datatype, distinct from routing flags. The method
named xor implements equality (XNOR); retain it even though the register example
uses other gates. Empty packet extent is one, routing windows use strict >, and
the sto distance stays 8*(bits-1)+5. Input updates preserve the right fold and
left-after-right overwrite order. The unused debug packet printer misnames its
arguments; actual tuple positions follow algorithm use.

The lazy variant memoizes signals, states, port/packet lists, tree nodes and
summary directions. The ignored scan-root reduction stays undemanded. The strict
variant constructs these finite values/spines eagerly. Both retain constructor/
depth guards and synchronous snapshots. Dff reads the previous clock's latch.
Signal and/or short circuit; identity gates retain cells. Input rows, padding
states, F/T values and packet values are shared. Unused label names stay deferred
in the lazy variant. Finite generators replace consumed prefixes of infinite
enumerations without changing selected values or order.

Output character streams remain memoized in both modes. Derived Show chooses F/T
by inspecting the Boolean, so GC's show-spine consumer still demands simulated
Boolean values, while leaving character heads unused. The printed consumer
forces those heads and its newline. Per-Boolean/punctuation checks run at the
same render-spine demand points. No later forced trace pass changes retention.

### Portable SML97 translation and adaptations

Retain state/port products, component/Boolean datatypes, packet tuples, scan trees,
maps, folds, transpose and immutable updates. A separate hold/load model is only
an oracle. The Signal class specializes to its sole active Boolean instance.
Standard SML records/products and memoized cells model source structures. Static
port descriptions use finite SML lists before suspended-list wrapping; this setup
translation is recorded. The measured simulator keeps functional state history.

Depth checks precede gate evaluation. Input gates can return Nothing without
demanding signals. Shared directional summaries and unused labels preserve
selective demand. Debug printers and unused input-enumeration helpers remain in
original source outside the runnable kernel. Sequential scans need no added
parallel runtime or compiler feature.

The shared driver reads profile arguments and a reviewed trace once, then
constructs/consumes a fresh circuit for every original iteration. Every Boolean,
structural character and EOF is validated without forcing unused character heads.
Printed mode additionally computes sum(ord output)+length over the original
newline-terminated characters. Controlled summary output replaces individual
writes; GC's original output remains empty. Report
repetitions:consumed-characters:head-checksum:source-output-bytes, with GC checksum
and byte fields zero. Decimal summary formatting happens after the work loop.
All added validation work is included in the identical SML compiler comparisons.

Selected identifiers, extents, distances, lengths, checksums and totals fit signed
31-bit Int. There is no reachable floating-point or arbitrary-precision arithmetic.
Normal/large retain width, clocks and all 97 source repetitions; smoke reduces
only repetitions to one. Default suite limits apply.

### Compiler/runtime diagnostic questions

Investigate prefix specialization, tree/record allocation, shared values,
short circuiting, selective forcing, retained clock state, eager/lazy metadata,
unused names, character-head demand and GC behavior. These are source hypotheses
until measurements establish effects. Comparisons use identical SML; Haskell
supplies correctness references. Counts/profiling, serial diagnostics and
headline timings retain separate scopes.

### Inputs, validation and references

Unmodified spectral executions match all three complete 97-line fixtures. GC
has no stored stdout fixtures and returns unit without output; its empty output
is checked as source behavior. Export-only observers from both copies agree on
full traces and shown lengths. Source versions and runtime flags are recorded.
An independent register model predicts previous stored bits with sto-selected
load/hold and agrees with five varied original traces at widths 1/2/3/8/16.

SML tests cover profiles/consumers, repeat formatting, varied data, wrong/truncated/
extra/checksum-colliding references, unused heads/labels, empty-input demand,
ignored root summaries, XNOR, inactive guards, routing boundaries, packet payload
demand and ragged transpose. Whole normal Rune O2 pilots retain 97 iterations
in all four combinations. Other host coverage belongs in validation.md.

[The pinned literate program](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/blob/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/circsim/Main.lhs)
establishes authorship, algorithm and sequential execution.

## circsim-strict

Evaluation: strict. Consumer: GC show spine only.

### Algorithm and workload

Simulate register circuits through the original immutable processor-state
records, port latches, packet lists and balanced-tree bidirectional scans.
Each clock stores inputs, sends depth-zero messages, evaluates/sends each path
depth, then restores request flags. Routing repeats until requests are acknowledged.
Preserve the register generator and padded processor count. Selected inputs are T.

### History, authorship, revision and aliases

The literate program credits David J. King and John O'Donnell, January 1998.
Its introductory email is dated 2 October 1998 and explicitly calls this sequential
code written with data-parallel combinators. The pin is nofib
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, gc/circsim/Main.lhs and
spectral/circsim/Main.lhs, their Makefiles and spectral stdout fixtures.
Complete source bytes are preserved. The files state no separate redistribution
notice; attribution does not infer a grant. The inventory recognizes the exact
literate authorship heading.

Full source comparison finds only the main consumer/comment different: GC forces
length(show(run ...)) then returns unit; spectral prints the shown trace.
Share the simulator implementation while retaining the inventory names circsim
(GC) and circsim-nofib (spectral), each with lazy/strict evaluation suffixes.
Their head demand and output work differ materially.

### Evaluation variants and source quirks

Signals use a separate F/T datatype, distinct from routing flags. The method
named xor implements equality (XNOR); retain it even though the register example
uses other gates. Empty packet extent is one, routing windows use strict >, and
the sto distance stays 8*(bits-1)+5. Input updates preserve the right fold and
left-after-right overwrite order. The unused debug packet printer misnames its
arguments; actual tuple positions follow algorithm use.

The lazy variant memoizes signals, states, port/packet lists, tree nodes and
summary directions. The ignored scan-root reduction stays undemanded. The strict
variant constructs these finite values/spines eagerly. Both retain constructor/
depth guards and synchronous snapshots. Dff reads the previous clock's latch.
Signal and/or short circuit; identity gates retain cells. Input rows, padding
states, F/T values and packet values are shared. Unused label names stay deferred
in the lazy variant. Finite generators replace consumed prefixes of infinite
enumerations without changing selected values or order.

Output character streams remain memoized in both modes. Derived Show chooses F/T
by inspecting the Boolean, so GC's show-spine consumer still demands simulated
Boolean values, while leaving character heads unused. The printed consumer
forces those heads and its newline. Per-Boolean/punctuation checks run at the
same render-spine demand points. No later forced trace pass changes retention.

### Portable SML97 translation and adaptations

Retain state/port products, component/Boolean datatypes, packet tuples, scan trees,
maps, folds, transpose and immutable updates. A separate hold/load model is only
an oracle. The Signal class specializes to its sole active Boolean instance.
Standard SML records/products and memoized cells model source structures. Static
port descriptions use finite SML lists before suspended-list wrapping; this setup
translation is recorded. The measured simulator keeps functional state history.

Depth checks precede gate evaluation. Input gates can return Nothing without
demanding signals. Shared directional summaries and unused labels preserve
selective demand. Debug printers and unused input-enumeration helpers remain in
original source outside the runnable kernel. Sequential scans need no added
parallel runtime or compiler feature.

The shared driver reads profile arguments and a reviewed trace once, then
constructs/consumes a fresh circuit for every original iteration. Every Boolean,
structural character and EOF is validated without forcing unused character heads.
Printed mode additionally computes sum(ord output)+length over the original
newline-terminated characters. Controlled summary output replaces individual
writes; GC's original output remains empty. Report
repetitions:consumed-characters:head-checksum:source-output-bytes, with GC checksum
and byte fields zero. Decimal summary formatting happens after the work loop.
All added validation work is included in the identical SML compiler comparisons.

Selected identifiers, extents, distances, lengths, checksums and totals fit signed
31-bit Int. There is no reachable floating-point or arbitrary-precision arithmetic.
Normal/large retain width, clocks and all 97 source repetitions; smoke reduces
only repetitions to one. Default suite limits apply.

### Compiler/runtime diagnostic questions

Investigate prefix specialization, tree/record allocation, shared values,
short circuiting, selective forcing, retained clock state, eager/lazy metadata,
unused names, character-head demand and GC behavior. These are source hypotheses
until measurements establish effects. Comparisons use identical SML; Haskell
supplies correctness references. Counts/profiling, serial diagnostics and
headline timings retain separate scopes.

### Inputs, validation and references

Unmodified spectral executions match all three complete 97-line fixtures. GC
has no stored stdout fixtures and returns unit without output; its empty output
is checked as source behavior. Export-only observers from both copies agree on
full traces and shown lengths. Source versions and runtime flags are recorded.
An independent register model predicts previous stored bits with sto-selected
load/hold and agrees with five varied original traces at widths 1/2/3/8/16.

SML tests cover profiles/consumers, repeat formatting, varied data, wrong/truncated/
extra/checksum-colliding references, unused heads/labels, empty-input demand,
ignored root summaries, XNOR, inactive guards, routing boundaries, packet payload
demand and ragged transpose. Whole normal Rune O2 pilots retain 97 iterations
in all four combinations. Other host coverage belongs in validation.md.

[The pinned literate program](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/blob/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/circsim/Main.lhs)
establishes authorship, algorithm and sequential execution.
[Blelloch's prefix-sum survey](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/afs/cs.cmu.edu/project/scandal/public/papers/CMU-CS-90-190.html)
provides scan background; [Partain](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17)
provides suite context. Parallel algorithm literature supplies background for
these sequential combinators.

## atom-lazy

Finite-value evaluation: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Produce a prefix of the one-dimensional atom state stream using the original
force law and explicit-Euler position/velocity updates. Keep positions and
velocities as finite lists. The timestep is binary32 0.02, spring parameter [1],
initial position [1] and velocity [0]. The source displays only positions, with
a tab per component and newline per state.

### History, authorship, revision and aliases

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/atom/Main.hs,
Makefile and all stdout fixtures. The header attributes the kernel to Ron Legere
at Caltech Quantum Optics. It records a historical Classic Hugs/GHC discrepancy
and relates it to commoning identical recursive calls. That anecdote is source
history rather than a current timing result. Full source and attribution bytes
are preserved; no separate redistribution notice is stated in these files.

Retain the established atom name with lazy/strict suffixes. The repeated
self-call is intentionally part of this benchmark; a shared self-referential
stream or linear state iterator would be a different implementation. The
independent linear iterator used for reference generation is confined to checks.

### Source quirks, sharing and evaluation variants

Each experiment invocation creates a distinct child experiment with identical
parameters. Its force law and propagation share that child stream, while the
outer stream remains separate. The initial state head is shared across calls.
Small counted-law probes check triangular force demands: for n displayed states,
lazy mode demands (n-1)*(n-2)/2 force heads (zero below two), while strict mode
demands n*(n-1)/2. These checks detect accidental stream knotting.

The source Num-list multiplication computes the first product, then multiplies
the RIGHT tail by itself, ignoring the left tail. Preserve that behavior; the
one-dimensional profile does not exercise it, so separate two-dimensional source
oracles do. Addition preserves the longer tail and its source matching order.
The force stream matches State at spine construction, but propagation leaves
its force-vector argument undemanded until velocity needs it.

The lazy variant suspends finite vector spines/elements and state fields.
The strict variant evaluates those finite values eagerly, including terminal
velocities not displayed by the source. Infinite state/force streams remain
memoized in both modes. The lazy consumer never forces an unshown velocity
solely for validation. A source bad-force probe displays two positions without
demanding force, then fails on the third; the lazy port preserves that behavior.

### Portable arithmetic, drivers and adaptations

Use the existing finite-normal binary32 helper shared with Mandel2. Values are
stored exactly in binary64 and rounded to 24 significand bits after each source
operation, ties to even. No optional Real32 structure or runtime feature is
required. Independent original-profile checks establish that every selected
operand/result is zero or normal; nonzero frexp exponents stay in [-18,2].
Products of binary32 operands need at most 48 significant bits; observed addend
exponent gaps are at most 19, so sums need at most 43. The binary64 intermediate
therefore represents these selected operations exactly before binary32 rounding.
The helper does not claim general subnormal/overflow/transcendental support.

Word32 encodes and checks every displayed position bit for bit. Masks, exponents,
indices and formatting counters have explicit bounded widths; signed zeros are
distinguished by the encoder. The initial timestep has bits 3CA3D70A. Each driver
invocation creates a fresh experiment instead of retaining the source top-level
test CAF across repeated suite invocations. Internal child-stream sharing is
retained. Profile arguments and the reviewed position file are read once.

Numeric formatting uses SML GEN9 instead of Haskell's shortest Float renderer.
Every numeric character is inspected, a binary32 roundtrip is checked, and tab/
newline lengths are consumed. Renderer-dependent text lengths are bounded rather
than exposed as cross-compiler expected output. Controlled output reports
position-count:rolling-bit-checkword, using explicitly modular Word32 xor/multiply
(seed 811C9DC5, multiplier 01000193). Every position is independently checked
against its fixture before contributing; this checkword does not replace checking.

### Compiler/runtime diagnostic questions

Investigate unshared recursive calls, within-invocation sharing, finite eager/
lazy vectors, unused velocities, closures, list temporaries, GC and whole-program
specialization. Emulated binary32 rounding and format validation are substantial
parts of this SML workload. Timing comparisons use identical SML across compilers;
GHC supplies correctness references. The source's historical compiler story does
not establish a performance explanation for current configurations.

### Inputs, correctness and references

| Profile | Displayed states | Input origin |
|---|---:|---|
| smoke | 100 | bounded prefix of the original FAST workload |
| normal | 2500 | unchanged NORM_OPTS |
| large | 4000 | unchanged SLOW_OPTS |

All three original 1000/2500/4000-state text fixtures remain in provenance.
Smoke uses 100 states to cover negative positions while keeping routine checks
bounded; normal/large keep the original parameters. Default limits apply.
Upstream text/bit observers agree with an independent linear binary32 Euler model
on all 4000 positions and velocities. Observers force velocities for auxiliary
checking; the primary lazy benchmark preserves the position-only demand.

SML probes check exact position/state bits, stream demand/triangular structure,
source vector quirks, sharing, ties to even, signed zero, finite-helper domain,
format roundtrip and wrong/short/extra references. Whole normal Rune O2 pilots
validate both policies at 2500 positions. Other coverage is recorded in validation.md.

[The pinned program](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/blob/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/atom/Main.hs)
provides the algorithm, attribution and historical explanation.
[Partain](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies nofib context.
[The SML Real interface](https://smlfamily.github.io/Basis/real.html) specifies the
rounding/conversion operations used by the helper. Source analysis, finite-input
bit checks and future performance explanations have separate evidence scopes.

on all 4000 positions and velocities. Observers force velocities for auxiliary
checking; the primary lazy benchmark preserves the position-only demand.

SML probes check exact position/state bits, stream demand/triangular structure,
source vector quirks, sharing, ties to even, signed zero, finite-helper domain,
format roundtrip and wrong/short/extra references. Whole normal Rune O2 pilots
validate both policies at 2500 positions. Other coverage is recorded in validation.md.

[The pinned program](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/blob/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/atom/Main.hs)
provides the algorithm, attribution and historical explanation.
[Partain](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies nofib context.
[The SML Real interface](https://smlfamily.github.io/Basis/real.html) specifies the
rounding/conversion operations used by the helper. Source analysis, finite-input
bit checks and future performance explanations have separate evidence scopes.


## exact-reals-lazy

Finite series evaluation: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Represent a constructive real by a function from requested binary precision to
an arbitrary-precision integer approximant. Evaluate the left-associated sum of
sin(i*pi), i=1..n, and render forty decimal places. The result is zero, but the
port performs the source exact arithmetic, range reduction and power series.
Nonzero scalar reference cases independently exercise its arithmetic.

### History, authorship, revision and notices

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/exact-reals/Main.hs,
Makefile and exact-reals.stdout. The header credits David Lester's 2012 paper,
[The world's shortest correct exact real arithmetic program?](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ic.2011.09.004),
Information and Computation 216, pages 39–46. Preserve the complete program and
fixture. These files state no separate redistribution notice. The suite retains
the established exact-reals name and gives meaningful evaluation variants
explicit lazy/strict suffixes.

Selected GHC base sources are pinned at 00920f176b0235d5bb52a8e054d89a664f8938fe.
Full base/LICENSE and the Ratio, Enum, List and Foldable sources preserve their
own notices. Their scope does not confer a notice on Lester's program.

### Evaluation, representation and translation

CR remains a precision-to-IntInf function. Function results are not memoized by
precision. Multiplication shares its two bound calculations within the CR value;
reciprocal repeats its precision search on every function call, as written.
Top-level pi, pi/2, pi/4 and sqrt(1/2) constructions and infinite coefficient
streams are memoized. Constants store CR functions, never precomputed answers.

The lazy policy suspends finite coefficient/power lists and their heads, stopping
at the first zero rounded term without forcing the unused tail. The strict policy
constructs those selected finite lists and evaluates their heads eagerly. Infinite
coefficient streams remain delayed in both. This policy deliberately exposes
otherwise unused series terms; the algorithm, bounds and requested precision stay
the same. No infinite list is made eager.

Keep the source left-associated sum. GHC.List/Foldable's list sum uses a strict
left fold; each CR addition still stores a function and requests two extra guard
bits from its operands. Reassociating or balancing the sum would change both work
and precision propagation. Enum CR uses the source default integer enumeration:
fromEnum evaluates at digitsToBits(40)=137, rounds to an integer, and toEnum
constructs each exact integer CR. The endpoints are not replaced by an unchecked
host loop convention.

Reuse the portable exact ratio operations shared with SCS. They follow GHC's
cross-product/reduction rules using IntInf, including normalization and gcd.
Each floor-square-root improvement constructs and normalizes its source ratio
before floor division. Rounding is floor(rational+1/2), with ties toward positive
infinity, including negative half integers. It is independent of host Real.round.
Only digitsToBits uses binary64 log/ceiling, yielding 137 for the selected forty digits. Full scalar and rendered
references are checked on every host. All integer precision counters fit signed 31-bit; arbitrary
precision intermediates retain IntInf.

Implement the source sine, cosine, atan branches, range reduction and square-root
path needed by this workload and auxiliary checks. Unused logarithm, exponential,
hyperbolic, reading and instance methods are omitted from the SML kernel; the
complete original remains. Finite SML strings replace Haskell output lists.
Read/validate arguments once per run, construct a fresh summation and compare
every rendered character with the forty-zero result before accepting it.
Coefficient/constant sharing persists across repeated in-process calls, as source
top-level definitions do; final sums are not cached. No runtime feature is added.

### Inputs, validation and calibration

| Profile | Summation endpoint | Origin |
|---|---:|---|
| smoke | 1 | small complete sum at unchanged forty digits |
| normal | 10 | calibrated complete sum at unchanged forty digits |
| large | 60 | original FAST_OPTS |

Upstream NORM_OPTS=350 and SLOW_OPTS=800 remain documented and available in
original reference evidence, but are not the suite normal/large choices. An
initial Rune stack pilot at endpoint 60 reached its 600-second limit before
finishing the lazy case; the combined pilot never started strict mode. This
records a time limit, not a wrong result. Endpoints 1 and 10 validate on both
policies at full precision. Large keeps the default 3600-second/8-GiB limit;
whole large SML validation is only claimed where separately recorded.

Rune's current IntInf library uses portable base-2^30 limbs and quotient-limb
search. This exact-rational workload is much more expensive there than on native
hosts with different big-integer implementations. Reducing digits, replacing
ratios with unchecked division or changing the summation would alter the workload;
they are not calibration changes. Profiles change n only.

Original GHC executions at 60/350/800 match the complete shared zero fixture.
Export-only observers record their 137-bit integer approximants as zero.
Fourteen scalar cases (pi, signed thirds, sqrt(1/2), trigonometric values and atan
across its branches) supply 84 exact integer approximants at six precisions and
14 forty-place texts. Both policies must match these source outputs exactly.
An independent 120-decimal-digit mpmath calculation checks integer error <=1
scaled unit and text error <=5.1e-41; this is a numerical cross-check, not a formal
proof. No floating tolerance replaces the primary exact output comparison.

Auxiliary tests cover half-integer rounding, first-zero stopping, unused inputs,
shared multiplication bounds, repeated reciprocal searches, left-addition
precision, small integer square roots, enum endpoints and the empty sum.
Primary smoke/normal matrices and counts use the manifest. Raw evidence and
validation scopes are recorded separately in validation.md.

### Compiler/runtime diagnostic questions and literature

Investigate arbitrary-precision arithmetic, gcd/normalization, function closures,
guard-bit propagation, coefficient sharing, early series termination, finite
eager evaluation, allocation lifetimes and whole-program specialization.
These are source-based hypotheses, not measured causal explanations. The common
SML program is the compiler comparison; original Haskell is a correctness
reference. Tiny or single-sample native runs are adapter diagnostics.

Lester's paper supplies the constructive-real algorithm and its error argument.
[Partain](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies suite context.
The pinned original and base sources supply the specific definitions translated
here; the independent high-precision check does not establish universal correctness.
